units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. If I only had a day. What are the five?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One. The Grand Place. A paved square, about sixty-eight meters by a hundred and ten, surrounded by guild houses with gilded decoration, and a Gothic town hall with a tower about ninety-six meters high.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The heart of the city.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And here's the surprise. Most of it isn't medieval.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In August of 1695, a French army under Marshal Villeroi shelled the city for two days, and most of the square was destroyed.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Only the stone shell of the town hall and a few fragments survived.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: But it looks perfect.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The guilds and owners rebuilt it in about four years.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So when you look at those golden facades, you're looking at a very fast, very proud recovery.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: UNESCO listed it in 1998.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Four years. My kitchen has taken longer.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Your kitchen didn't have the guilds competing.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Fair. Number two.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Manneken Pis. A small bronze boy, about fifty-five centimeters tall, relieving himself into a fountain basin on a street corner, a few minutes from the Grand Place.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And I bet you a coffee that you'll say "that's it?" out loud.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Everyone does. People are always disappointed by how small he is.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I win.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You haven't even been there yet.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But he has a wardrobe of about a thousand costumes, which have their own museum nearby.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A thousand outfits. For a statue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And there are two or three competing legends about why he exists.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: My favorite is the baby duke of Leuven, who supposedly relieved himself on enemy troops from a basket in a tree.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A tiny duke, in a tree, in a basket.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Winning a battle.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Number three.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A glass-roofed shopping arcade, opened in June of 1847, designed by an architect named Jean-Pierre Cluysenaar.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's about two hundred and thirteen meters long and has three sections.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The King's, the Queen's, and the Princes' galleries.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And it's still a shopping arcade?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: With chocolate shops, a theater, a cinema, bookshops, and the Taverne du Passage.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's also where the Lumière brothers' films were shown in public in Brussels, in 1896.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Number four.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Boulevard Anspach and the Bourse.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Underneath that wide pedestrian boulevard, the Senne is still flowing, in a tunnel.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: They buried a river.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Between 1867 and 1871. The river was polluted and flooded, so the city covered it over and built grand boulevards on top, modeled on Paris.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Bourse, the old stock exchange, went up between 1868 and 1873.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And since 2015, the boulevards around it have been mostly car-free.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A river under a pedestrian street.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Brussels does like to hide things.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And five. The Atomium.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: The giant atom.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A giant steel model of an iron crystal, built for the 1958 World's Fair.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You can ride up inside it for a view over the city.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's out on the northern edge, so it's a metro ride away.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's a half-day trip.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. So pick one or two of these and enjoy them, rather than rushing through all five.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Rushing through Brussels. Never works.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Never.
